subject: Cert-broker patterns for private domains & DNS delegation
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Cert-broker patterns for private domains & DNS delegation

Hi Alice / SecOps team —

Thanks again for the deeper dive yesterday. Per our call, I put together a short proposal for how Redwood Private would handle TLS and DNS for your private endpoints (VPC + on-prem connectors). The core idea is a lightweight "certificate broker" service that centralizes issuance, rotation, and audit for private FQDNs while preserving your ownership of DNS zones and KMS. High-level points below; attachments include a diagram and a short pros/cons doc.

Key proposal elements (summary):
- Certificate broker (Redwood-managed service running in customer VPC or as a sidecar) that requests certs from either customer CA (via protocol X) or public CA (ACME) depending on policy.
- DNS: Customer retains authoritative control. We request short-lived certs using a DNS-based validation handshake; for on-prem the broker can use a signed CSR flow instead.
- Termination: Mutual TLS at the internal load balancer for inter-service traffic; TLS passthrough to customer-managed edge if required for compliance.
- Rotation: Broker enforces automated rotation windows, publishes rotation events to your audit log (S3/Cloud log) and integrates with your KMS/HSM for private key protection.
- Trust model options: internal CA chain vs. per-host SANs vs. wildcard certs (tradeoffs in revocation surface and ease of rotation).

Open questions for you:
1) Do you want Redwood to manage private keys (we'll store them encrypted and rotate) or hold keys in your HSM and only sign CSRs?
2) Will you accept ACME-style DNS validation for internal zones, or require an explicit CSR+approval flow?
3) For tenant FQDNs, do you prefer per-tenant certs (more isolation) or a delegated wildcard (simpler ops)?

Action items I propose: quick security review of the diagram (attachment), then a 30‑minute workshop to lock in choices and an implementation plan.

Tagged attachments: cert-broker-diagram.png, acme-vs-ca-pros-cons.pdf, dns-delegation-checklist.md

Subject: Re: Cert-broker patterns for private domains & DNS delegation

Marissa — thanks for the clear summary and the diagram. A few quick clarifications from SecOps side: we prefer that private keys for our production tenant FQDNs remain in our HSM; we can sign CSRs on request. DNS: internal zones are managed by our on-prem DNS team and we cannot allow external DNS updates.

Specific asks:
- Can the broker support a CSR + signed-certificate return flow (no external DNS TXT records)?
- We need detailed audit events (who requested cert, which CLI/API user triggered rotation) pushed to our SIEM in a structured format (JSON).
- For multi-tenant staging, we accept wildcard certs; for prod we require per-tenant certs with key material in HSM.

If you can support CSR/HSM signing and structured audit events, we can proceed. Suggest a short workshop next week with your infra owner (Karthik) and our DNS/HSM engineers.

Regards,
Alice Nguyen
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Analytics
alice@acme-analytics.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Cert-broker patterns for private domains & DNS delegation

Alice — great, thanks for the direction. Quick replies inline and a proposal for next steps.

1) CSR + HSM: Yes — the broker will accept signed CSRs from your HSM. Implementation model: customer-side agent (small binary or Terraform provider) generates CSR inside HSM, sends signed CSR to broker over mTLS, broker validates policy and returns signed cert. Private key never leaves HSM.

2) Audit events: we'll emit structured JSON events to a connector you configure (Syslog/HTTP/S3). We'll include user, principal, cert fingerprint, operation, and timestamp. We'll also write an optional webhook for immediate rotation alerts.

3) Per-tenant prod certs: supported. We'll include rate limits and a per-tenant quota table in the attachment. Wildcard for staging is fine.

Attached: updated cert-broker-diagram.png (added HSM flow), and a short DNS delegation checklist.

Proposed workshop times (30 min):
- Tue May 18 10:00-10:30 PT
- Wed May 19 14:00-14:30 PT

Marissa / Mina — can you host the call and walk through the diagram? Alice — which slot works for your team?
